newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean lawmaker admits taking money from Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean lawmaker admits taking money from Hanbo.

text.p: A leading South Korean opposition member of parliament said on Wednesday he had taken money from the founder of the troubled Hanbo Group, which is at the centre of a loan scandal.

Kwon Roh-kap, a close associate of opposition leader Kim Dae-jung, told reporters that he had accepted between 150 million and 160 million won ($173,000-$184,000) from Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo since 1993.
Kwon said the money was used to finance his election campaigns. "But I have nothing to do with preferential lendings to Hanbo," he told reporters.
He is the first politician to admit taking money from Chung, who was arrested on Friday over the loan scandal which has rocked South Korea.

Hanbo Steel, flagship of South Korea's 14th largest conglomerate in South Korea, had piled up about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions before it was declared insolvent on January 23.

State prosecutors have questioned officials of the Hanbo Group and its creditor banks over a lobbying fund kept by Chung and examined the conglomerate's bank accounts to find out if there were irregularities.
